result:
None of the three final answers matches the value I get from a consistency check, though I did not prove the result rigorously.

**Sanity check at h = 1.** In PG(3,q), the bound becomes (t−2)q + t. An elliptic quadric (an ovoid) has q²+1 points, and every plane meets it in at most q+1 points. Setting t = q+1 gives (q−1)q + q + 1 = q²+1, so the bound is attained at t = q+1.

**Generalising to h.** The analogue of an ovoid is a set of q^{2h}+1 subspaces. Requiring (t−2)q^h + t = q^{2h}+1 gives t = q^h + 1. This reduces to q+1 when h = 1, so it is the natural candidate. I did not rule out other forms that also reduce to q+1 at h = 1, such as q^{h−1}(q+1).

**Checking the solutions.**
- Solution 1 gives q−1. At h = 1 the ovoid forces t = q+1, so this is wrong.
- Solution 2 gives q^h−1. This also fails at h = 1, where it gives q−1.
- Solution 3 gives q^{2h}. At h = 1 it gives q², which does not match q+1, so it is wrong.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
